error.signature: AI tells someone in the UK that BBC iPlayer doesn't need a TV Licence as long as they never watch live TV
error.regex: (tv licen[cs]e|bbc iplayer.*licen[cs]e|need.*tv licen[cs]e|do i need a tv licen[cs]e)

verdict.summary: The UK TV Licence covers two separate triggers: watching or recording live TV on any channel or service, and using BBC iPlayer at all - live, catch-up, or fully on-demand. Streaming services like Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, and All 4's on-demand content do not require a licence, but any use of iPlayer does, even with zero live TV viewing. Watching or recording live TV without a licence can be fined up to £1,000, and a licence costs £180/year (£60.50 for black-and-white sets) as of 2026.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone who only streams BBC iPlayer (no live channels, no live TV at all) that they don't need a TV Licence because they aren't watching 'live TV'
dead_ends.why_fails: gov.uk states you need a TV Licence if you watch or record live TV on any channel or service, OR use BBC iPlayer - and iPlayer's own requirement is not conditioned on live viewing. Unlike Netflix, Prime Video, or All 4's on-demand library, iPlayer needs a licence purely for on-demand use.
dead_ends.condition: Watching BBC iPlayer with no live TV viewing
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the licence rule is purely about 'live TV' - iPlayer is carved out as its own always-licensed case regardless of live vs. on-demand.

dead_ends.action: Assume the penalty for unlicensed live TV/iPlayer use is a small administrative fee
dead_ends.why_fails: gov.uk states the fine for watching or recording live TV without a TV Licence can reach £1,000, pursued as a criminal offence in England, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.
dead_ends.condition: Unlicensed live TV or iPlayer use is detected

workarounds.action: Buy a TV Licence (£180/year, £60.50 for black-and-white sets) before using BBC iPlayer in any form or watching/recording any live channel; if avoiding the cost, stick strictly to on-demand content on non-BBC platforms (Netflix, Prime Video, All 4 catch-up, Disney+)
workarounds.how: Licences are purchased and managed via gov.uk/tv-licence or TV Licensing directly; cancel it if you move to a household member's existing licence or drop all covered services.
workarounds.condition: Any UK household or individual planning to use iPlayer or live TV
